spec.title: WireGuard packet rate
spec.description: Received and transmitted packets per second on the WireGuard interface for peer $clusterid. High pps with a small average packet size means the CPU is spending most of its time handling interrupts, not moving bytes.

spec.title: Average packet size
spec.description: Average packet size = bytes / packets for peer $clusterid. Values well below the path MTU (for example under 500 bytes) while latency is high indicate a packets-per-second problem rather than a bandwidth problem.

spec.title: Interface drops
spec.description: Packets dropped on ingress/egress of the WireGuard interface for peer $clusterid. Non-zero values mean the interface queues could not accept traffic.

spec.title: Interface errors
spec.description: Receive and transmit errors on the WireGuard interface for peer $clusterid. Look here for framing, CRC, or length problems.

spec.title: Interface FIFO errors
spec.description: RX/TX FIFO (ring-buffer) errors on the WireGuard interface for peer $clusterid. These indicate the driver ring buffer overflowed, which is another sign that the receive/transmit path cannot keep up.

spec.title: Softnet time squeeze
spec.description: Number of times per CPU the NET_RX softirq exhausted its budget with work remaining. Increasing values while latency grows confirm the softirq worker cannot keep up.

spec.title: Softnet backlog length
spec.description: Current number of packets waiting in the per-CPU netdev backlog. If this number grows and stays high, packets are queueing in the kernel, which directly increases latency.

spec.title: Softnet dropped packets
spec.description: Packets dropped because the per-CPU netdev backlog was full. Non-zero values mean the backlog overflowed and packets were lost.

spec.title: Softnet processed packets
spec.description: Total packets the NET_RX softirq processed per CPU. Use this as the baseline pps the kernel interrupt handler is dealing with.

spec.title: UDP buffer errors
spec.description: UDP-level drops from /proc/net/snmp, scoped to the gateway pod network namespace for peer $clusterid. RcvbufErrors means the WireGuard UDP socket receive buffer was full; SndbufErrors means a send buffer was full. These are the most direct proof of UDP socket buffer saturation.

spec.title: UDP socket queue bytes and buffer limits
spec.description: Current bytes queued in the WireGuard UDP socket send/receive queues and the configured maximum UDP buffer sizes (rmem_max / wmem_max) for peer $clusterid. Use this panel to see buffer pressure in real time together with its ceiling.
